public_rationale: The ASU paper version available August 5, 2025 reported declining reasoning effectiveness as training and test transformations differed more in controlled synthetic tasks [e1]. An April 2025 study reported improved generalization on tested code-reasoning tasks, including mutated programs [e2]. Apple's June 2025 paper reported accuracy collapse as puzzle complexity increased, without establishing distribution shift as the cause [e3]. These studies document task-specific failures and improvements, but do not connect them to identified development efforts and their missed capability targets [e1, e2, e3]. They therefore neither establish nor displace the proposed explanation for recurring frontier-model development shortfalls [e1, e2, e3].

Results on selected tasks do not establish a common cause across development efforts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Failure to generalize outside the training distribution is the principled reason efforts to build GPT-5-level models keep missing their target.

statement.excerpt: And, crucially, the failure to generalize adequately outside distribution tells us why all the dozens of shots on goal at building “GPT-5 level models” keep missing their target. It’s not an accident. That failing is principled.
statement.document_title: GPT-5: Overdue, overhyped and underwhelming. And that’s not the worst of it.

from_speaker: failure to generalize adequately outside distribution
all the dozens of shots on goal
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that a systematic weakness in handling unfamiliar problems explains recurring failures to achieve the broad capabilities sought from frontier models.
The claim concerns development efforts up to the post on 2025-08-09. It is not a forecast that no future model can overcome this weakness.
“Principled” means a recurring technical limitation, rather than an accidental failure. It need not mean that distribution shift is the only contributing cause.

Marcus supplies neither a capability threshold for “GPT-5 level” nor a list of the development efforts and their targets. Selected benchmark failures can test the proposed mechanism but cannot alone establish the full causal attribution.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations show that distribution shift systematically causes relevant reasoning failures, and evidence connecting those failures to the development efforts establishes that this weakness explains their recurring shortfalls against documented capability targets.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence from the relevant development efforts shows that their missed targets occurred despite adequate generalization on the capabilities at issue, with controlled tests or development records identifying a different explanation that displaces the proposed common cause.

evidence.publisher: Chengshuai Zhao and colleagues, Arizona State University; arXiv
evidence.explanation: The controlled synthetic experiments support the proposed distribution-shift mechanism within their tested setting. They do not identify the claimed development efforts, establish their targets, or show why those targets were missed.

evidence.publisher: Rem Yang and colleagues, MIT and Brown University; arXiv
evidence.explanation: Tests across ten models found improved generalization on code-reasoning tasks, including mutated and generated programs intended to probe distribution differences. This limits a blanket inference of generalization failure, but success on these tasks does not establish adequate broad generalization or resolve the claimed cause of missed development targets.

evidence.publisher: Parshin Shojaee and colleagues, Apple; arXiv
evidence.explanation: The study establishes failures on controlled puzzle tasks as complexity increases. It does not isolate training-distribution mismatch as their cause or connect them to the development efforts Marcus describes.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Document the relevant development efforts and targets through August 9, 2025. Obtain controlled tests and development records showing whether distribution-shift failures explain their shortfalls, or whether adequate generalization and another demonstrated cause displace that explanation.
